title: I have lost a day
author: Suetonius

translation: And once at dinner, remembering that he had done nothing for anyone the whole day, he made that memorable and rightly praised remark: "Friends, I have lost a day."
translation_note: praestitisset is subjunctive because it gives Titus's own reason, as he thought of it. perdidī is a perfect: "I have lost" (the day is gone).

essay.t: Suetonius opens his Life of Titus by calling him "the love and delight of the human race".
Yet he also reports that before Titus became emperor, people suspected him of cruelty, luxury and greed, and openly said he would be another Nero.
The Life is built on that reversal.

Our passage closes a section about his generosity as emperor: Suetonius says Titus confirmed his predecessors' grants in a single edict instead of making people petition again, and never let anyone leave without hope.
When his household warned him that he promised more than he could deliver, he answered that no one ought to go away sad from a conversation with the emperor.
Then comes the remark at dinner: having done nothing for anyone that day, he said he had lost it.
The historian Eutropius, in his short summary of Roman history, gives it as "Amici, hodie diem perdidi", adding hodie, "today", and he too calls Titus the love and delight of the human race.

I did not find the anecdote in the surviving text of Cassius Dio on Titus, which I checked in translation; that absence does not make it false, but it means our evidence rests on Suetonius and his followers.
Dio offers a useful caution: Titus's good record, he suggests, may also have been due to the fact that he lived only a very short time after his accession.
Suetonius gives the length of the reign as two years, two months and twenty days, and says Titus died in his forty-second year.

A reputation for generosity built over twenty-six months is easier to keep than one tested over decades, so the saying tells us at least as much about how Titus was remembered as about how he governed.

questions.q: What made Titus say he had lost a day?
options: He had done nothing for anyone that day
He had been ill all day

questions.q: What caution does Cassius Dio offer about Titus's reputation?
options: It may owe something to his very short reign
He was actually crueller than Nero
It was based on forged letters
